content.text: No customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or early-termination fees appear anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties or minimum/early-termination fees on Sparkling (the Customer). Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay fees "as set out in the Fee Schedule" with no late-payment interest or penalty mechanic, and Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination fee or payment of remaining contract value. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "interest", "damages" and fee/charge language returned no Customer-payable stipulated sums; the only "penalties" reference (p0090) is within Garman's indemnity of Sparkling, and the non-solicitation clause (Section 19) carries no fee for breach. Amounts flowing on termination run in our favour (Garman returns fees paid under Sections 8(b) and 17(c)). This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is required.
